S3-DG1.entrypoints: Distinguish existing-source collection anchoring, new collection creation, fresh exact-payment reversal and committed replay. Slice 3 reversal must reuse existing validated original collection evidence, never create an original collection as an implicit side effect.
S3-DG1.discovery: Before writes, freeze the branch, Order, actor, customer, exact source payments/collections, current Cash Shift when needed and every Shift referenced by rows actually being inserted. S3-DG1.acquisition: Authorize first; acquire exact operation idempotency gates, then phase4-order gate. Acquire required Shift rows in UUID order before the Order/payment/collection rows. Current Cash Shift uses FOR UPDATE; historical FK-only Shift uses FOR KEY SHARE. For a shared identity use the strongest required mode up front, never upgrade later. Acquire planned remaining FK parent key locks before the first evidence INSERT.
S3-DG1.contention: Use NOWAIT for preplanned business/FK row acquisition so a full-Shift reversal holding Shift/order resources cannot create a blocking inverse cycle. Contention is an explicit rollback/retry outcome, not success or a masked timeout. Replay remains read-only and does not take these business locks.
S3-DG1.freshValidation: After locking, reread all identities/statuses and compare the plan. Any new Shift, branch/source relationship or missing lock means rollback/safe retry, never late discovery/acquisition. No client-visible result is committed before validation.
S3-DG1.legacyHelperBoundary: The current Migration 120 helper discovers/locks only one current Shift and therefore is not sufficient for multi-Shift FK plans. Future additive private prelocked routines must reuse the established root domain and Slice 2 evidence/identity validation while consuming the frozen plan. They must not call the old blocking discovery helper after later locks, including the CliQ/no-open-Shift case where a new Shift could appear.
S3-DG1.proofRequired: Real independent-session tests for historical A/current B versus full reversal of A and B, inverse UUID ordering, Shift close/open during discovery, no-open CliQ, FK parent contention and post-lock relationship changes. Measure deadlock delta and prove loser content-sensitive zero footprint; no static measured-deadlock claim.

S3-DG2.population: Build an exact disjoint per-Order source population from validated modern sale/completion facts and exact public customer_payments. Reject unsupported tenders, ambiguous legacy evidence, unrepresented payments and contradictory source bindings rather than infer truth from orders.amount_paid or an incomplete private SUM.
S3-DG2.initialCollections: Migration 115 POS stores original net collection in its immutable business-operation result without inserting a customer_payments row. Migration 116 Customer completion can either store a full initial collection without a payment row, or reference a partial collection by customer_payment_number. A partial completion linked to that exact payment contributes once through the payment source, not again through the completion result. Full initial modern collection is a distinct source fact, not a fabricated customer payment and not an extra reversible payment under this slice.
S3-DG2.sourceIdentity: Use typed source identity: validated original modern sale/completion operation versus exact original customer_payment_id. Revalidate original operation/request/result/order bindings; resolve Customer partial payment_number to its unique payment and verify order/amount/tender/actor relationship. Missing or contradictory anchors are unsupported/fail-closed.
S3-DG2.foundationAuthority: Slice 2 collection evidence may describe an already-committed authoritative source payment and is not a second inflow. All prior private reversal events used in operational coverage require exact validated coordinator completion and movement evidence. A foundation-only prior reversal makes the Order population ineligible; do not ignore it or adopt it as an operational outflow.
S3-DG2.candidate: Before writes, validate the full source population and every prior operational reversal/settled Return. Compute tender-independent coverage from distinct committed source collections minus validated operational reversals, then subtract the one exact candidate payment. Preserve the approved debt/refund/delivery equations; monetary refunds constrain reversible capacity and are not subtracted twice or used to recreate debt.
S3-DG2.writerBoundary: Migration 124 SUM-only capacity is insufficient for this expanded population. Future additive coordinator/prelocked writer logic must calculate candidate capacity from the complete typed source set instead of blindly delegating capacity to the closed Slice 2 helper. Original Slice 2 implementation stays unchanged/private. Public writer and financial reader convergence remains a separate activation prerequisite.

newCollection.request: Derive actor from the authorized session; freeze a versioned actor/order/amount/actual tender/reference/notes request before async work. Cash/CliQ only, exact minor-unit integer bounds, contract-specific reference validation, required actor/key ownership, explicit NULL/JSON-null rejection. Normalize only declared request fields; same key with a different normalized request conflicts.
newCollection.identity: A public new-payment attempt is not the existing-source anchor identity in Migration124: that identity already includes originalPaymentId and omits public notes. Add an immutable outer request/result envelope linked bijectively to the server-generated customer_payment, its exact collection event and validated source operation. Preserve the closed anchor contract rather than pretending its request was the public request. Internal anchor keys are server-owned and cannot be claimed through the public input namespace.
newCollection.transaction: One preplanned transaction creates the source payment with its idempotency identity, exact source/collection evidence, operational completion, audit, derived projection and stored public result. Deferred total relational validation must reject incomplete source/evidence/envelope states at commit. No source-only receipt or foundation-only outcome becomes operational success. Sequence gaps are not partial business effects.
newCollection.lockPlan: Authorization and immutable request first; serialize exact actor/key, check committed identity, then the existing phase4-order root gate. Freeze Shift/FK/source membership and strongest modes, acquire the sorted Shift set before Order/payment/evidence resources, prelock all actor/customer FK parents, and fresh-revalidate before writes. Reuse the approved NOWAIT/retry model; a new Shift or relationship never causes late earlier-rank acquisition. The new source primitive consumes a validated held plan; it must not call the old public writer or recursively enter a coordinator after later locks.
newCollection.completionCallers: Customer partial completion already calls the non-once payment path from inside its parent transaction. Align that parent to preplan the complete source/evidence/FK set and use a private prelocked primitive with a deterministic parent-owned receipt identity. Validate the original completion/source binding after the parent result is present; do not recursively acquire a new idempotency/root gate after inventory or child locks. POS/full Customer initial collection remains its original typed source, not a fabricated customer payment.
newCollection.replay: Authenticate and validate actor/key/request plus the committed envelope and durable relational evidence before current eligibility/Shift checks. Return the immutable stored result, including its original execution-time balance/timestamps. No new anchor, receipt, projection repair, evidence or money write on replay. New action requires a new explicit business-attempt identity.
newCollection.oldKeyCompatibility: Probe both the new envelope and existing unique customer_payments(created_by,idempotency_key) domain before any fresh business write. One historical owner/key match must match all provable persisted order/amount/tender/reference/notes fields; mismatch conflicts, ambiguity fails closed. Preserve a compatible receipt lookup as explicitly historical/legacy receipt replay, never as a Phase5 coordinator completion. Historical remaining was reconstructed from current state by Migration078, not stored: identify it as a current informational legacy field or unsupported, never manufacture an original immutable result/fingerprint. A reversed or incomplete historical receipt cannot silently become fresh eligibility or new success. New operational replay requires actual committed operational evidence.
newCollection.legacyAdmission: Preserve historical rows and proven historical receipt/Legacy read contracts. Canonical mutation requires complete supported typed source evidence for the entire sale. Unsupported tender, legacy reversed flag, ambiguous creation/completion or missing evidence produces explicit unsupported/incomplete capability and no guessed coverage. Cash/CliQ-only NEW inputs do not relabel historical card/bank_transfer/cheque rows, erase them from discovery or authorize canonical adoption. Existing source-anchoring remains audit evidence, not a new inflow.

paymentIntentContract.sharedBoundary: A payment-specific adapter for customerAccounts.service and RecordCustomerPaymentModal, modeled on the closed aftercare recovery architecture but with its own versioned storage namespace, action, request/result validators and error allowlist. Do not change the closed aftercare implementation or reuse an aftercare key.
paymentIntentContract.immutableRequest: Synchronously copy raw input before the first async boundary. Parse the decimal amount exactly into positive integer minor units without floating-point rounding; reject unsupported precision/range, missing order, and new tenders other than cash/cliq. Canonicalize only approved whitespace/null conventions for reference and notes. Bind the resulting versioned request, order, action=customer_collection, actor, intent UUID, attempt UUID, stable idempotency key and fingerprint. Auth validation must confirm the actor captured for the record; auth changes invalidate submission, not rebind it to another actor.
paymentIntentContract.persistence: Persist and read back PREPARED before any RPC submission; storage failure or unavailable secure UUID generation prevents submission. Store multiple attempts by immutable attempt identity, with an actor/order action index and generation, status, hadUnknownOutcome and validated result. Browser records contain no tokens and are consistency evidence, never financial authority. Retain successful and unresolved identities rather than overwriting one pending slot with a new action.
paymentIntentContract.stateMachine: PREPARED -> IN_FLIGHT before sending; a crash/reload of IN_FLIGHT is conservatively OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. A complete relationally validated committed result -> SUCCEEDED. Transport loss, cancellation, timeout, malformed response, or stale/unbound response cannot prove rollback and -> OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. An allowlisted server SQL rejection may yield DEFINITIVELY_REJECTED only if this attempt has no earlier unknown/in-flight ambiguity; later rejection cannot erase hadUnknownOutcome. Otherwise keep OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and recover the same key or require review.
paymentIntentContract.intentTransitions: START_NEW creates a new intent/key only on explicit operator action after checking there is no unresolved overlapping actor/order attempt. A later identical legitimate payment after validated prior success is a new intent, not a replay. RECOVER_EXISTING loads and validates the original stored request/key; changed form state is ignored for recovery and must never create a key implicitly. Definitive rejection with no unknown history permits a later explicit START_NEW; unresolved history blocks it until authoritative resolution.
paymentIntentContract.reloadAndTabs: Use actor/order/action browser serialization around durable state transitions and generation compare-and-set. Re-read ownership/key/fingerprint/generation after every await and before publishing a result. Another tab's newer generation cannot be overwritten by an older response. Web Locks coordinate same-origin tabs only; database actor/key uniqueness and shared key-domain conflict checks remain final cross-device authority. Missing browser coordination must fail closed for mutation, not silently fall back to uncontrolled parallel writes.
paymentIntentContract.migrationEraRecovery: A pre-upgrade pending attempt without a durable original key/request cannot be safely reconstructed from amount/time/order similarity. Surface REVIEW_REQUIRED and prohibit automatic resubmission/new-key inference. An exact known old key may use the separately authorized historical receipt lookup; no-match alone is not proof that an old in-flight attempt cannot commit. This is a manual evidence-resolution boundary, not permission to invent receipts or backfill facts.
futureRuntimeProof: Commit payment30 on capacity100, drop response, reload and recover exact key: one receipt30 and unchanged replay fingerprint, not a second30 under another key
Pre-send storage failure; crash after IN_FLIGHT; loss before/after commit; rejection after unknown history; auth change and edited form during auth/lock wait
Two tabs, delayed/reordered result, multiple historical successful attempts plus one unresolved attempt, explicit later identical new payment and cross-actor storage isolation
Old pending attempt without identity blocks guessing; old exact known key returns receipt-only evidence and never operational adoption

paymentResponseContract.newBoundary: Define a versioned public collection RPC and capability-aware payment adapter, separate from the unversioned six-argument legacy once signature. The exact proposed new signatures are now specified in activationManifestProgress.newInterfaceSignatures and require independent confirmation before implementation; do not activate a JSON contract behind a stale caller that treats every error-free reply as success.
paymentResponseContract.operationalSuccess: Versioned discriminant COMMITTED_COLLECTION with success=true, actorId, orderId, action, idempotencyKey, requestVersion, requestFingerprint, full normalized request, operationId, originalPaymentId, collectionId, paymentNumber, immutable committed amount/method/reference/notes, and immutable outstandingBefore/outstandingAfter minor-unit values. replay is transport metadata, not a changed business result. Stored outcome is bound one-to-one to the exact payment/collection/source-operation and must pass durable relational validation before first success or replay.
paymentResponseContract.financialValidation: Minor-unit JSON values are canonical non-negative decimal strings in the PostgreSQL bigint range; positive collection amount must equal the frozen request exactly. No Number coercion, unsafe integers, NULL-to-zero defaults or absent-field defaults. At settlement outstandingBefore >= amount and outstandingAfter = outstandingBefore - amount. These are original committed position values, not the current balance on a later replay. Display conversion cannot change stored money. Current financial position, if separately fetched, is informational and never substituted into immutable replay.
paymentResponseContract.postRpcValidation: Require the exact version/discriminant, success flag, valid identifiers, captured actor/order/action/key/fingerprint, normalized request equality and amount/tender/reference/notes equality. Validate the committed position arithmetic and nonempty receipt identity. Recheck local attempt generation/identity before CAS persistence. Unsupported, receipt-only, error-free success:false, unknown schema, malformed money or mismatched identity can never persist SUCCEEDED or trigger the payment-success toast.
